niches_top.name: Fish otolith (ear-stone) image & chemistry archives
niches_top.score_justification: Raw images + chemistry, dozens of lab collections, reader-vs-reader age gap, known-age anchors exist.

fidelity_card.RAW: High-resolution otolith photographs and LA-ICP-MS / isotope transect files on lab and institute sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One fish specimen — hundreds per collection, dozens of species, same imaging protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Age read by reader A vs reader B vs chemistry; usually only published means survive
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Known-age hatchery fish and bomb-radiocarbon validated ages

niches_top.headline_shape: A stone inside a fish's head has recorded every winter of its life — and two experts reading it can disagree by years.
niches_top.why_niche: Age labs keep their own image piles; there is no central reconciliation product, only per-lab atlases (AFORO, national collections) that never joined each other's readings.

niches_top.name: Weakly electric fish EOD waveform recordings
niches_top.score_justification: Raw .wav is the specimen; species-specific signal; taxonomy rewritten by DNA after recordings were filed by ear.

fidelity_card.RAW: Uncompressed .wav/.mp3 electric-organ-discharge recordings with oscillogram exports, on lab and personal research sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One recorded fish — hundreds of individuals, dozens of species per expedition, one electrode protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Species named by waveform at capture vs later DNA-barcode revisions of the same vouchers
fidelity_card.ANCHOR: Museum voucher specimens tied to recording numbers

niches_top.headline_shape: A fish that 'sees' with electricity broadcasts its own name in a waveform — and the recordings were filed under names DNA later changed.
niches_top.why_niche: A handful of labs (Cornell mormyrids, Crampton's gymnotiforms) hold expedition piles on their own sites; no cross-lab EOD library exists.

niches_top.name: Frog & toad call archives (regional fonotecas)
niches_top.score_justification: The task's own example: raw .wav/.mp3 per species, regional sound libraries, call IDs vs DNA-split species.

fidelity_card.RAW: Original .wav/.mp3 advertisement-call recordings with accession numbers, on regional fonoteca and lab sites
fidelity_card.UNIT: One calling male — thousands of accessions per fonoteca, hundreds of species, standard field-recorder protocol
fidelity_card.LABEL_GAP: Call filed under the species name at recording vs the DNA-split taxonomy of today (second ruler)

niches_top.headline_shape: A frog smaller than your thumbnail has a unique voice — and thousands of taped voices are filed under species that have since been split in three.
niches_top.why_niche: Fonoteca Zoológica (Madrid), Fonoteca Neotropical and university piles each hold their own accessions; the big platforms host photos, not these accessioned raw calls.
